name: Kakadu National Park
note: National park: a World Heritage park of about 20,000 km2 in the Top End, the destination visitors base from for its walks, rock art, waterfalls and billabongs.

name: Jabiru
note: Town: the park's gateway, with the Bowali Visitor Centre, supermarket, lodging and services, and the base for Ubirr and Nourlangie.

name: Cooinda
note: Settlement and lodge on the Yellow Water road, the pick-up point for Yellow Water cruises and park tours.

name: Gunbalanya
note: Community (Oenpelli) across the East Alligator River, reached with a permit, where the Injalak Arts centre and the Injalak Hill tours start.

name: Yellow Water
note: Billabong (wetland) on the East Alligator River floodplain, cruised by boat from Cooinda: the park's best-known wildlife landmark, with birds and crocodiles.

name: Ubirr
note: Rock art site with a short walk through galleries and a climb to a sunset lookout over the floodplains.

name: Nourlangie Rock
note: Rock art shelter and lookout on the Burrungkuy (Nourlangie) road, with a 1 km walk past galleries and the sandstone escarpment.

name: Nanguluwur Art Site
note: Rock art gallery near Nourlangie Rock with hand stencils and spirit figures, on the Nanguluwurr walk.

name: Jim Jim Falls
note: Waterfall: the park's tallest, at the end of a 4WD track and a walk across rocks; a plunge pool with sand beaches in the dry season.

name: Twin Falls
note: Waterfall in the Arnhem Land escarpment reached by a boat shuttle up the gorge, with a walk to the plateau above.

name: Gunlom
note: Waterfall and plunge pool at the top of a steep climb in the south of the park, with views over the park from the pools.

name: Maguk
note: Waterfall and rock pools (Barramundi Gorge) in monsoon rainforest in the south of the park, with a bush campsite nearby.

name: Motor Car Falls
note: Waterfall in monsoon forest on Motor Car Creek, a swimming spot reached on a 7.5 km return hike, mainly in the wet season.

name: Koolpin Gorge
note: Gorge (Jarrangbarnmi) of waterholes and waterfalls in the south-east, reached by 4WD tour or permit with a limited number of visitors.

name: Bowali Visitor Centre
note: Visitor centre in Jabiru with interpretive displays on Kakadu's ecology and Aboriginal culture, a gallery and a film; the park's main information point.

name: Warradjan Aboriginal Cultural Centre
note: Cultural centre at Yellow Water with exhibits on the traditional owners' story of the park and a shop with local art.

name: Mamukala Wetlands
note: Wetlands with an easy 300 m bird hide walk and a 3 km loop, one of the best bird-watching spots, 30 km from Jabiru.

name: Anbangbang Billabong
note: Billabong on a 2.5 km loop walk near Nourlangie, a spot for birds and wildlife with a view back to the rock.

name: Nawurlandja Lookout
note: Lookout on a short climb near Nourlangie, a popular sunset viewpoint over the escarpment.

name: Cahills Crossing
note: Tidal causeway on the East Alligator River, the usual place to watch estuarine crocodiles from the bank.

name: Mirrai Lookout
note: Lookout at the top of a 3.6 km return walk to the Mount Cahill viewpoint over the escarpment, from the Mirrai carpark south of Bowali.

name: Bardedjilidji Walk
note: Easy 2.5 km walk through sandstone outliers and woodland beside the East Alligator River, with an ancient occupation shelter.

name: Manngarre Rainforest Walk
note: Short wheelchair-friendly 1.2 km return walk through monsoon rainforest starting at the East Alligator River downstream boat ramp.

name: Gubara Pools
note: Six-kilometre return walk to shady monsoon forest pools with butterflies and a swim, 9 km along the Nourlangie road.

name: Barrk Sandstone Walk
note: Challenging 12 km walk off the Nourlangie lookout track past the main rock art gallery and sandstone country, 6 to 8 hours.

name: Yurmikmik Walks
note: Series of interconnected walks in the south of the park to waterfalls and swimming holes, including Boulder Creek and Motor Car Falls.

name: Kungarre Walk
note: Kungarre Monsoon Forest and Billabong Walk: 3.6 km return walk at South Alligator to Ankurdabbal Billabong, with birdlife.

name: Home Billabong
note: Billabong viewing platform on a 1.8 km return floodplain walk near Yellow Water, best from July to November.

name: Nadab Lookout
note: Lookout on the climb above Ubirr over the Nadab floodplain, a stop on the Ubirr visit.

name: Bukbukluk Lookout
note: Lookout walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Budjmi Lookout
note: Lookout walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Mirray Lookout
note: Lookout walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Mardukal Billabong
note: Billabong walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Kungardun Walk
note: Walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Yilikadjarr Walk
note: Walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Bubba Wetlands Walk
note: Wetlands walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Barrk Marlam Walk
note: Walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Badbong Wodjmeng Sandstone River Walk
note: Sandstone river walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Bowali Track
note: Walk in the park's walks list, named by Parks Australia, from the Bowali Visitor Centre area.

name: Jim Jim Billabong
note: Billabong near Jim Jim Falls named in the park's birdwatching list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Alligator Billabong
note: Billabong named in the park's birdwatching and crocodile list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Red Lily Billabong
note: Billabong beside a camping area on the park's birdwatching list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Bucket Billabong
note: Billabong beside a camping area on the park's birdwatching list, named by Parks Australia.

name: Marrawuddi Arts & Culture
note: Gallery and cultural centre in Jabiru, one of the park's listed galleries.

name: Injalak Arts
note: Art and craft centre in Gunbalanya where Kunwinjku artists paint and weave, with a gallery and shop; the start of the Injalak Hill tours.

name: Injalak Hill
note: Rock art hill near Gunbalanya with x-ray style art shelters, visited only on Traditional Owner-guided morning tours from Injalak Arts.

name: Arnhem Land
note: Region: Aboriginal-owned land across the north-east of the Top End with its own permit system, the name Tourism NT and Wikivoyage use for the area beyond Kakadu.

name: Nhulunbuy
note: Town on the Gove Peninsula, the main base in East Arnhem Land with shops, services and the start of the local sights.

name: Roy Marika Lookout
note: Lookout on the summit of Nhulun (Mount Saunders) a short walk from town, with views over the wetlands, harbour and coast.

name: Gayngaru Wetlands
note: Wetlands walk through paperbark forest in town with bird hides and viewing platforms, a Yolngu hunting site.

name: Wirrwawuy
note: Sand dunes at Cape Wirrawoi, 5 km from town, for sunrise and sunset photographs.

name: Middle Beach
note: Casuarina-shaded beach between Wirrwawuy and East Woody Beach, popular for family walks and fishing.

name: Galuru (East Woody Beach)
note: Beach with white sand and rust-red cliffs near Nhulunbuy, a sunset spot and the walk-out point for East Woody Island.

name: Dhamitjinya (East Woody Island)
note: Island reached by a sandspit walk from East Woody Beach, with 360-degree views of the coastline.

name: Gadalathami (Town Beach)
note: Beach closest to Nhulunbuy, facing the Gulf of Carpentaria, for evening walks.

name: Garanhan (Macassan Beach)
note: Beach 35 minutes from town with Yolngu stone pictures of Macassan trade, picnic tables and camping with a permit.

name: Banambarrna (Rainbow Cliffs)
note: Sheer 40 m coloured laterite cliffs near Gove Airport, viewed from the beach below; the top is a sacred site and is closed to visitors.

name: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre
note: Art centre, gallery and museum in Yirrkala with Yolngu bark paintings, carvings and the original church panels, 19 km from Nhulunbuy.

name: Bremer Island
note: Island 15 minutes by air or an hour by boat from Nhulunbuy, with beach strolls and day cruises and the Banubanu Beach Retreat.

name: Lonely Beach (Bawaka Homelands)
note: Remote white-sand beach on an azure inlet at the Bawaka homelands, reached only with a tour or permit.

name: Garig Gunak Barlu National Park
note: National park covering the Cobourg Peninsula, its beaches, islands and waters, with Black Point and Victoria Settlement; reached by air, sea or 4WD with a permit.

name: Victoria Settlement
note: Ruins of an 1838 British military outpost at Port Essington, with stone ruins and headstones, reached by boat or tour.

name: Black Point Cultural Centre
note: Ranger station and cultural centre at Black Point (Algarlarlgarl) in Garig Gunak Barlu, on the area's Aboriginal, Macassan and European history.

name: Umbakumba Art Centre
note: Cultural and art centre on Groote Eylandt, a way to experience Indigenous culture on the island.

name: Groote Eylandt
note: Island in the Gulf of Carpentaria, Anindilyakwa land, reached by air or sea, with art centres and the Alyangula settlement.

name: Maningrida
note: Remote Aboriginal community on the north coast with a lodge and art, reached with a permit; a gateway, not a sight on its own.
